polly_note: DATA-ONLY REFRESH (Thursday 2026-07-30). Decision review: Mondays. No verdicts today. The EN A/B test remains CONCLUDED from the 07-28 review (dead heat, promote neither) and is not re-litigated. THREE THINGS THIS MORNING. (1) GERMANY HAS ITS FIRST CONVERSION. The DE page took 1 transaction this week (193 sessions), bringing post-fix cumulative to 233 sessions and 1 transaction. This resolves the zero-conversion worry in the least dramatic way possible: it was noise, exactly as the arithmetic predicted. At an EN-like 0.8 percent the 233 sessions predicted about 1.9 conversions and we observed 1, so DE is running low but is no longer an anomaly that needs explaining. I am deliberately NOT upgrading this to 'DE works'. One conversion is one conversion. The honest read is that the page is now inside the range where a real rate can eventually be measured, and it needs several more weeks of volume before anyone compares it to EN. (2) THE BOUNCE RISE HAS PERSISTED FOR A SECOND READING, so it is no longer a one-week blip. A is 79.9 percent and B is 81.5 percent, against roughly 70 to 72 percent two weeks ago. Both variants remain locked together, which continues to point at traffic mix rather than a page regression. Still not diagnosed, and diagnosis is a Monday job, but it has now earned a proper look rather than a watch note. (3) SHOPIFY IS STILL DOWN, SO SALES FIGURES ARE UNCHANGED AND STILL UNCONFIRMED. Both delegated connections continue to reject the access token, tested again this morning. real_sales_90d has deliberately NOT been rolled forward or re-dated; it carries the same origin-unconfirmed warning as yesterday. Nothing regional, including the German page thesis, should be decided until this is fixed and the numbers are re-pulled by someone who can name the source. GERMAN PAGE: v2 published for Lucas after his design feedback. While building it I caught myself inventing two payment methods (giropay and Sofortueberweisung) that the live store does not offer; I verified the real set against the storefront and corrected the page. Two claims on it still need Lucas to confirm before it could ever go live: whether pay-by-invoice is actually enabled, and whether 'ships from the EU in 4 to 8 working days' is accurate.

built_not_yet_live.name: German LP v2 - brand-matched, trust-led
built_not_yet_live.note: v2 PUBLISHED 2026-07-30 after Lucas's design feedback on v1. Now uses the real LP design system (navy/gold/cream, Cinzel and Raleway) instead of an approximation, fixes product images that were being cropped out of proportion, drops the 'Recommended for Germany' badge, and rewrites the German with proper umlauts (v1 used ASCII workarounds like 'gross' and 'Laender', which reads cheap to a German reader and was probably much of why it looked wrong). Trust content is built around what a German buyer actually checks before ordering from abroad: ships from the EU with no customs, 4 to 8 working days with tracking, 14-day statutory right of withdrawal, prices marked inkl. MwSt., and Impressum plus Widerrufsbelehrung in the footer. CORRECTION MADE DURING THE BUILD: the first draft listed giropay and Sofortueberweisung as payment methods. Neither is offered. I verified the real set against the live storefront (PayPal, Klarna, SEPA, Visa, Mastercard, Maestro, Amex, Apple Pay, Google Pay, Shop Pay) and removed the invented ones. TWO CLAIMS STILL NEED LUCAS TO CONFIRM BEFORE THIS COULD GO LIVE: whether pay-by-invoice is actually enabled in Klarna (the single strongest German trust lever, currently left off the page because it is unverified), and whether 'ships from the EU, 4 to 8 working days' is accurate. UNDERLYING THESIS STILL UNVERIFIED: the page leads with the Base Game on the assumption Germany wants a lower-risk entry, and the country-by-product split needed to test that is still blocked on Shopify access.
